# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 88 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 88 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_088_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 5

**1** The shepherd came and said to the virgins, "Have you done this man any harm?" "Ask him," they said. I replied, "Lord, I was very glad to remain with them." **2** "What did you eat?" he asked. "Lord," I said, "I ate the words of the Lord the whole night." **3** "Did they treat you well?" "Yes, Lord," I replied. **4** The shepherd smiled and said to me, "Do you know the name of the tall man?" "No, Lord," I said. "It is the Son of God," he answered. **5** "But why does he appear as a tall man?" I asked. "Because he is taller than the tower," he said. **6** "Tell me also about the gate, Lord," I said. "Listen," he said: "this gate is the Son of God — this is the only entrance to the Lord. No one shall enter in to him except through his Son. **7** Did you see the six men and the glorious and great angel in the midst of them? He is the Son of God, and the six are the glorious angels who support him on right and left. **8** None of these glorious angels enters the presence of God without him; whoever does not take his name upon himself shall not enter the kingdom of God." **9** "But what is the tower?" I asked. "The tower," he said, "is the church." **10** "And these virgins — who are they?" "They are holy spirits, and no one can be found in the kingdom of God unless these clothe him with their garment; for if you receive the name alone but do not receive from these their garment, you shall not profit." **11** "And the white garments of the virgins — what are they?" "They are their names," he answered. "If anyone who bears the name of the Son of God also bears all these names, he shall enter the kingdom of God."

---

### Translator's Note
This is the doctrinal apex of the Tower Vision. The triple identification — gate = Son of God, rock = Son of God, tower = Church — constitutes one of the earliest systematic ecclesiologies in Christian literature. The dual requirement for kingdom entry (name/baptism + virtues/garments) is the central pastoral message. Verse 6's exclusivity formula anticipates the developed Fourth Gospel christology. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout; PNEUMA's paraphrase in v. 6 is theologically accurate but slightly expands the Greek.
